s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic right-sided chest pain with worsening on inspiration, accompanied by severe sweating and cold sensation, in a patient with a history of interstitial pneumonia
salient_findings: Right-sided chest pain worsening with inspiration
Severe sweating confined to the right arm and thoracic area
Cold sensation on the right side
Pleural friction rub over the right chest
Decreased surface temperature over the right arm and right thorax
key_facts: 74-year-old man
History of interstitial pneumonia
One month of right-sided chest pain
Severe sweating on the right arm and thoracic area
Cold sensation on the right side
Pleural friction rub over the right chest
Vital signs: blood pressure 150/78 mmHg, pulse 71/min, respiratory rate 20/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Chest CT showed dense infiltrates in the ventral subpleural regions of the right upper and middle lobes
Oral antibiotic therapy failed to improve the infiltrates
No history of smoking, trauma, or asbestos exposure
Medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and varicose veins
Laboratory tests showed a white blood cell count of 9,000/μL and C-reactive protein of 1.14 mg/dL
Bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage revealed macrophages 65.1%, lymphocytes 4.8%, neutrophils 29.9%, and eosinophils 0.2%
Transbronchial lung biopsy showed no malignancy or specific inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of severe sweating on the right arm and thoracic area, cold sensation, and decreased surface temperature over the right arm and right thorax corresponding to dermatomes C5–T12 are consistent with sympathetic dysfunction, and the presence of a pleural friction rub and dense infiltrates in the ventral subpleural regions of the right upper and middle lobes on chest CT suggest a possible apical lung lesion, but the lack of malignancy or specific inflammation on transbronchial lung biopsy and bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage makes Pancoast tumor or lung cancer less likely
